questions.question: Which Claude subscriptions include Claude Code, and what first-party local authentication modes exist?
Which Claude Code mechanisms are documented for scripts or CI, and what deployment limits apply?
What Claude credential-sharing, lifecycle, revocation, API-billing, and third-party-wrapper constraints apply?
Which ChatGPT plans include Codex and what local, device, API-key, and access-token sign-in modes exist?
Which Codex plan-backed credentials are documented for trusted non-interactive workflows or runners?
What Codex restrictions apply to copied login state, shared runners, concurrency, rate limits, and continuous audits?
Which account classes and authentication modes currently apply to Gemini CLI?
Can Gemini CLI plan-backed credentials be used headlessly on persistent brokers or custom runners?
Is Google Antigravity automatable through official CLI or SDK surfaces, and how does its authentication differ from Gemini CLI?
Which OpenCode subscription providers and plan-backed routes are documented, and which are workarounds or terms-hostile?
Can OpenCode run unattended while isolating credentials and preserving upstream provider identity?
What is supportable for GitHub Copilot when used through OpenCode?
Does Grok Build have official CLI, headless, SDK, or API automation surfaces?
Is plan-backed Grok Build use officially supportable outside first-party interactive use, and what lifecycle, fair-use, and model evidence is exposed?
What authentication posture applies to OpenRouter as an API fallback?
Which workstation, OS-user, VM, self-hosted-runner, GitHub-hosted-runner, and manual-app deployments are supportable per tool?

findings.claim: The supplied host probe was static-only: all model-capable live invocations were NOT_RUN, plan-auth provenance remained UNKNOWN, and no observed model identity was established. External vendor research extends deployment policy but does not change those local observations.
findings.decision_impact: No local CLI may be treated as plan-backed or unattended-ready merely because it is installed or logged in.

findings.claim: Anthropic documents Claude Code subscription OAuth for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise accounts, alongside API-key and cloud-provider authentication modes.
findings.decision_impact: Claude Code can be considered for plan-backed local use, but the inspected host's current auth mode remains UNKNOWN.

findings.claim: Anthropic documents claude setup-token as a long-lived OAuth credential intended for CI pipelines, scripts, and non-browser environments; the documented token lifetime is one year.
findings.decision_impact: First-party Claude Code plan-backed automation is supportable with limits when this explicit mechanism is used and isolated.

findings.claim: Anthropic Workload Identity Federation and service-account mechanisms are API-side workload credentials using short-lived tokens; they are not evidence of subscription-plan billing.
findings.decision_impact: API workload identity must remain a separate route from plan-authenticated Claude Code.

findings.claim: OpenCode's provider documentation states that Anthropic prohibits using Claude Pro or Max subscription authentication through OpenCode and removed bundled support for that route.
findings.decision_impact: Treat Claude subscription authentication through third-party wrappers as blocked unless Anthropic provides direct written authorization.

findings.claim: OpenAI sources disagree on the complete plan list: the Help Center states Codex is included across ChatGPT plans including Free and Go, while developer-facing pages foreground Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise.
findings.decision_impact: Entitlement must be checked against the current workspace plan; the discrepancy does not affect the distinction between ChatGPT sign-in and API billing.

findings.claim: Codex CLI documents ChatGPT browser sign-in, device-code authentication, API-key authentication, cached auth reuse, and access-token authentication.
findings.decision_impact: Plan-backed and API-billed Codex routes can be separated explicitly in adapter configuration.

findings.claim: OpenAI documents Codex access tokens for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise trusted non-interactive local workflows, scheduled jobs, CI runners, and app-server clients, with configurable expiry and administrator revocation.
findings.decision_impact: Business or Enterprise access tokens are the strongest official plan-backed Codex credential for a trusted private runner.

findings.claim: OpenAI documents copied auth.json reuse only as an advanced trusted-runner flow and recommends API-key authentication for programmatic workflows; plan usage is subject to rolling usage windows and possible additional limits.
findings.decision_impact: Personal-plan cached auth should remain operator-triggered and serialized, not a shared generic runner credential.

findings.claim: Google states that from June 18, 2026 Gemini CLI stopped serving consumer-tier requests for Gemini Code Assist for individuals and Google AI Pro or Ultra through Login with Google.
findings.decision_impact: Consumer Google AI Pro or Ultra plan authentication must not be selected for Gemini CLI automation.

findings.claim: Gemini CLI authentication documentation still describes cached Google-login credentials for supported account classes, but says fresh headless authentication without cached credentials must use a Gemini API key or Vertex AI credentials.
findings.decision_impact: Workspace or Code Assist cached-login use may remain viable on a named workstation, but unattended broker and runner support is not established by these sources.

findings.claim: Google Antigravity has official first-party CLI and SDK surfaces, including documented silent authentication and enterprise Google Cloud integration.
findings.decision_impact: Antigravity is not manual-app-only, but deployment classification still depends on credential lifecycle and runner guidance.

findings.claim: Public Antigravity documentation reviewed did not establish precise subscription-token storage, lifetime, revocation, or supported persistent and ephemeral runner classes.
findings.decision_impact: Keep Antigravity plan-backed execution operator-triggered until lifecycle and deployment permission are documented.

findings.claim: OpenCode documents headless run and server modes and stores provider credentials in a per-user local data directory, allowing OS-user or VM isolation at the wrapper layer.
findings.decision_impact: OpenCode can be isolated technically, but this does not authorize any particular upstream subscription route.

findings.claim: Because OpenCode is a third-party adapter, upstream provider terms and credential rules remain controlling; OpenCode's technical support cannot convert a prohibited or undocumented provider route into a supported one.
findings.decision_impact: Every OpenCode plan-auth route requires provider-specific authorization before unattended deployment.

findings.claim: OpenCode documents GitHub Copilot device login, while GitHub requires a licensed GitHub account and prohibits sharing a single user login among multiple people.
findings.decision_impact: Named-user workstation use is supportable with limits; copied shared-runner session state remains UNKNOWN and should be blocked.

findings.claim: xAI documents Grok Build for interactive TUI use, headless scripts or bots, and ACP integration. In non-browser environments, the explicit documented authentication route is XAI_API_KEY.
findings.decision_impact: Grok Build headless execution is official, but the clearest unattended credential is API-billed rather than plan-backed.

findings.claim: The reviewed xAI sources did not establish subscription-session token lifetime, revocation, credential portability, or permission for persistent or ephemeral self-hosted runners.
findings.decision_impact: Plan-backed Grok Build should remain first-party and operator-triggered; use API keys for unattended automation.

findings.claim: OpenRouter is an API-billed fallback using bearer API keys, per-key credit limits, management API keys, and OAuth flows that ultimately issue or store API keys.
findings.decision_impact: OpenRouter is supportable as API fallback only and must not be represented as plan-backed authentication or identity authority.

findings.claim: No vendor documentation in this track proves the actual model used by any local invocation, and the local probe ran no model calls.
findings.decision_impact: Requested or displayed model names cannot satisfy provider-attested identity or independence requirements.

contradictions.conflict: OpenAI sources present different complete lists of ChatGPT plans that include Codex.
contradictions.next_evidence: Current plan-specific entitlement page or workspace admin documentation that reconciles Free, Go, Plus, Pro, Business, Edu, and Enterprise.

contradictions.conflict: Gemini CLI authentication documentation still describes Google-account login while a newer deprecation removes consumer Google AI Pro, Ultra, and individual Code Assist service from Gemini CLI.
contradictions.next_evidence: Treat the deprecation as controlling for consumer tiers and the authentication guide as applicable only to remaining supported account classes.

contradictions.conflict: The strongest explicit statement that Anthropic plan auth is prohibited in OpenCode comes from OpenCode documentation rather than an Anthropic terms page reviewed in this track.
contradictions.next_evidence: Direct Anthropic legal or product documentation, or written vendor clarification, covering third-party Claude Code clients and subscription OAuth.

contradictions.conflict: Antigravity has first-party CLI and SDK surfaces, but Google's FAQ recommends Vertex AI or AI Studio API keys for third-party coding agents using Gemini.
contradictions.next_evidence: Preserve the scope distinction: first-party Antigravity plan use is separate from third-party Gemini-agent authentication.

contradictions.conflict: xAI officially advertises headless Grok Build, but the explicit non-browser authentication path is API-key based and subscription-session runner permission is not documented.
contradictions.next_evidence: xAI documentation or written policy covering unattended plan-authenticated Grok Build and self-hosted runner deployments.

unknowns.question: How is a Claude Code setup-token explicitly revoked before expiry, and is there an admin inventory for all such tokens?
unknowns.why_unknown: The reviewed public authentication page established lifetime and purpose but not a complete revocation-management workflow.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Automated Claude Code deployment requiring immediate centralized revocation.
unknowns.next_evidence: Current Anthropic admin documentation or vendor clarification for setup-token inventory and revocation.

unknowns.question: What exact concurrency and machine-copy limits apply to personal-plan Codex cached authentication?
unknowns.why_unknown: Official docs describe trusted-runner reuse and serialization guidance but do not establish a general personal-plan service-account model.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Parallel or shared personal-plan Codex runner pools.
unknowns.next_evidence: OpenAI plan terms or product documentation explicitly covering machine count, concurrency, and unattended personal-plan automation.

unknowns.question: Which Workspace or Gemini Code Assist licenses permit persistent plan-backed Gemini CLI brokers or custom runners?
unknowns.why_unknown: Consumer tiers were deprecated, while remaining organization account classes and cached-login behavior are not mapped to runner permissions.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Plan-backed Gemini CLI automation outside a named workstation.
unknowns.next_evidence: Google Workspace or Gemini Code Assist administrator documentation explicitly covering non-interactive runners.

unknowns.question: What are Antigravity subscription credential storage, lifetime, refresh, revocation, and runner-class rules?
unknowns.why_unknown: Public documentation reviewed exposes CLI, SDK, silent auth, and enterprise integration but not a complete lifecycle contract.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Persistent or ephemeral Antigravity plan-backed workers.
unknowns.next_evidence: Antigravity authentication and administrator lifecycle documentation.

unknowns.question: Do OpenAI and GitHub explicitly authorize their subscription credentials inside OpenCode for unattended automation?
unknowns.why_unknown: OpenCode documents technical provider integration, but matching first-party vendor permission for unattended OpenCode use was not located.
unknowns.blocking_scope: OpenCode plan-backed Codex or Copilot runner deployment.
unknowns.next_evidence: First-party OpenAI and GitHub documentation naming OpenCode or a general third-party-client automation policy.

unknowns.question: What lifecycle, revocation, sharing, and fair-use rules apply to plan-authenticated Grok Build sessions?
unknowns.why_unknown: xAI public pages reviewed emphasize headless capability and API-key deployment but not subscription credential governance.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Unattended plan-backed Grok Build on any runner.
unknowns.next_evidence: xAI authentication, account, and automation terms specific to Grok Build subscriptions.

unknowns.question: How can each tool produce provider-attested actual model identity and billing-route evidence per run?
unknowns.why_unknown: No live invocation was allowed and product login state does not itself attest the model or billing route used.
unknowns.blocking_scope: Independence claims, proof normalization, and plan-backed billing assertions.
unknowns.next_evidence: Bounded later receipt collection under an approved live-probe protocol, plus vendor-documented identity fields.

unknowns.question: What unpublished fair-use or abuse thresholds could affect continuous high-frequency subscription audits?
unknowns.why_unknown: Public limits and terms do not expose all anti-abuse heuristics or suspension thresholds.
unknowns.next_evidence: Vendor enterprise agreement, support confirmation, or published automation policy.

unknowns.question: Can plan credentials be provisioned directly into a dedicated local OS account or VM without copying workstation session state?
unknowns.why_unknown: Some vendors document device or browser login and some document automation tokens, but a uniform dedicated-account portability contract does not exist.
unknowns.next_evidence: Per-vendor provisioning and administrator documentation for dedicated machine identities.

recommendations.recommendation: Permit plan-backed Claude Code automation only through first-party Claude Code authentication, preferring setup-token for scripts or CI; block Claude subscription auth through OpenCode or other wrappers.
recommendations.rationale: Anthropic documents a dedicated first-party automation token, while third-party subscription use carries explicit terms risk.
prerequisites: Dedicated OS user or worker secret boundary

recommendations.recommendation: Use Codex Business or Enterprise access tokens for trusted non-interactive plan-backed workers; keep personal-plan cached auth operator-triggered, private, and serialized.
recommendations.rationale: Access tokens are the clearest official plan-backed automation credential; copied personal auth is an advanced and fragile path.
prerequisites: No forked or public PR execution

recommendations.recommendation: Reject consumer Google AI Pro or Ultra authentication for Gemini CLI; use API key or Vertex AI for unattended Gemini CLI, and treat Workspace or Code Assist plan-backed runners as blocked pending documentation.
recommendations.rationale: Google ended consumer Google-login service for Gemini CLI on June 18, 2026 and documents API or Vertex authentication for fresh headless environments.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep Antigravity plan-backed use operator-triggered on a named workstation or isolated local user until token lifecycle and runner-class support are documented.
recommendations.rationale: Official CLI and SDK surfaces exist, but lifecycle and unattended deployment permission remain incomplete.

recommendations.recommendation: Treat OpenCode as an adapter, not an auth authority: enable only API routes or subscription routes explicitly permitted by the upstream provider.
recommendations.rationale: Technical integration cannot override provider account or credential terms.

recommendations.recommendation: Limit GitHub Copilot through OpenCode to a named licensed user on a workstation until GitHub documents unattended third-party runner use; do not copy one user's session into a shared pool.
recommendations.rationale: Device login is documented, but account sharing is prohibited and OpenCode-specific unattended authorization is not established.

recommendations.recommendation: Use Grok Build plan authentication only for first-party operator-triggered local sessions; use XAI_API_KEY for unattended headless workers.
recommendations.rationale: Headless use is official, but API keys are the explicit non-browser auth path and subscription runner governance is unknown.

recommendations.recommendation: Use OpenRouter only as API fallback with separate per-environment keys, hard credit limits, and management-key isolation.
recommendations.rationale: OpenRouter is an API routing surface, not a plan-authentication or model-identity authority.

recommendations.recommendation: Map UNKNOWN, CONFLICTING, or merely cached interactive credentials to non-executable states; allow manual or operator-triggered receipts instead of unattended execution.
recommendations.rationale: The campaign explicitly rejects converting technical possibility into permission.

recommendations.recommendation: Require every future run receipt to record tool, auth class, plan-versus-API billing route, credential owner, deployment class, requested model, observed model evidence, and revocation handle.
recommendations.rationale: Local installation, cached login, and displayed model labels are insufficient proof.

synthesis_implications: The external research does not alter the local OBSERVED state: all current model-capable CLI auth modes and actual models remain UNKNOWN until a separately approved live receipt exists.
Claude Code and Codex have the strongest documented plan-backed non-interactive credential surfaces, but only inside explicit first-party and trusted-runner constraints.
Gemini CLI consumer plan authentication is not a viable automation route after June 18, 2026; Workspace or Code Assist runner permission remains a carried unknown.
Antigravity and Grok Build have official headless or programmatic surfaces, but their plan-auth credential lifecycle and runner permission are not documented sufficiently for unattended deployment.
OpenCode must remain an adapter whose eligibility is the intersection of its technical capability and the upstream provider's terms.
OpenRouter remains API fallback only and cannot attest subscription use, provider identity beyond returned metadata, or audit independence by itself.
Dedicated OS-user or VM isolation is necessary but not sufficient; vendor authorization and credential lifecycle evidence are separate gates.
A cached browser or device login is not automatically a sanctioned CI credential.
Unknown revocation, sharing, concurrency, fair-use, or actual-model identity must fail closed rather than silently promote to a runner route.
No token-to-plan-credit conversion is established in this track.
